items.title: Tim Ries interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, March 19, 2022
items.q: President Carter invited us to play at the Carter Center so we played there.

ctx.x: Wow that’s definitely putting me on the spot. Well I try — the first thing you hear from a person is their voice, right? I mean so whether you’re talking or singing or almost like — so you know the appealing nature of sounds, so I feel like okay the first thing you have is like the ability hopefully to translate — and I tell this to young musicians, I’ve had students over the years, talking about you are the instrument. Because the saxophone is just a piece of metal. You can put a different mouthpiece and…

sounding thing and I’m playing a wooden mouthpiece so I try to have the like low resonance of — so I don’t know, I mean I do my best to humanize it and, you know, in all of this thing I should just maybe end with saying about this ensemble that I have called the Universal Spirits Ensemble and it’s a group of musicians — it was originally for the idea of the conflict that was happening with the Israeli-Palestinian-Lebanese because I figured okay this is thirty years ago but now the world is just everything is…
A tradition of that with jazz ambassadors. So thank you for today and for last night. And congratulations on your career so far and whatever you’re going to do next.
